solves.myAnswer: both complex and collaborative. while the queen is certainly treated like a royal, with an entourage of her children tending to her every need, bees make big decisions democratically, not by royal decree. when a colony gets too large, a group of some thousands of bees will split off and create a new colony. but deciding where to establish a new home is no simple task for these intelligent and opinionated insects. to come to an educated group decision, they set up a temporary camp and send scouts to explore the surrounding areas, relating accounts of their journeys upon their return through the language of interpretive dance. other bees then set out on a property viewing with the scout whose dance they found most compelling, after which they return and present their own dances for those who remain undecided. after many rounds of 'voting', the location that gathers majority support becomes the site of the new colony
